change.task: Follow-up of the PR #811 review: confirm the writer stop despite Docker races and slow daemons, and close three paths that left writers running
change.origin: Soak 40155878690 (manual dispatch from dev) failed closed after 14.5 h. The Docker writer stop at the end of a segment counted a failed docker inspect or docker kill of a container that exited during the stop as a failed stop, although no writer remained.
change.driver: stop_node_writer_commands kills each owned container directly after its inspect confirms the owner. A failed inspect or kill is a failure only when a second docker ps still lists the container as running. A failed docker ps, a failed host-control stop-owned, an invalid container ID, or another owner label still fails the stop. The end-of-segment stop has its own budget SOAK_WRITER_STOP_SECONDS (5 to 120 s, default 30 s). After a host protection breach or during an emergency it keeps DISK_STOP_SECONDS. writer-stop-failure.txt names the failed step, the container, and the Docker error. A confirmed stop with output keeps it as writer-stop.log. The exit cleanup stops the owned writers when the driver exits before the end-of-segment stop. A pytest that a signal ends gets its owned writers stopped before the evidence copy. The target_advanced early exit record starts with its reason, and early-exit.txt is read once.
change.host_control: stop-owned and prefer-oom write one line on stderr for each process that they skip because its environment is unreadable. The owner scan returns the skipped PIDs. Behavior does not change. The unit tests that need an unreadable environment return early when they run as root.
change.fixture: test-run-merge-recovery-soak.sh adds a fake docker with four owned containers, a FAKE_STOP_DELAY setting, and the cases slow, vanish, exits, stuck, persist, sigkill, breach, and breach-inspect. The target_advanced case checks the reason prefix and a restart that keeps the reason.

guarantee_change.before: At the end of a segment, any failed docker inspect or docker kill of an owned container failed the stop, also when the container had exited. The stop had the emergency budget of 1 to 5 s. An exit between iterations skipped the stop, and the writers of a signal-ended pytest ran until the end of the segment.
guarantee_change.after: The stop fails only when a container stays listed as running after the kill, or when docker ps, host-control stop-owned, a container ID, or an owner label fails its check. Each confirmed container stops before the next inspect. The end-of-segment stop has a 30 s default budget outside emergencies. An exit before the end-of-segment stop and a signal-ended pytest also stop the owned writers.
limitation: The driver does not confirm the owner label of a container that exits before its inspect. A container that docker ps does not list as running does not write.
The end of a segment can take up to SOAK_WRITER_STOP_SECONDS plus 1 s longer than before.
The stop after a signal-ended pytest records a failure only in the writer-stop.log of that iteration. The end-of-segment stop decides the result of the soak.
Like the end-of-segment stop, the exit stop applies only to a soak without a Casper manifest (SOAK_INPUT_DIR not set), and only before the end-of-segment stop has run.

review_findings.finding: stop_node_writer_commands inspected every owned container before it sent any kill. Four one-second inspects used the 2 s emergency budget. An isolated Linux comparison left all four containers running, while the base stopped two. Each later stop attempt during the breach repeated the delay.
review_findings.resolution: 85b04c07e kills each container directly after its inspect confirms the owner. The Docker CLI sends one request for each inspected container, so a batched inspect would not remove the delay. The breach-inspect case failed on 1250e8490 and passes on 85b04c07e and on the base.
